title: Orphaned content snapshot coordinator reacquires the post-store write freeze
fault_primitive: MongoDB fsync write lock reacquired by a detached administrative shell in an existing remote container
incident_class: Leftover backup maintenance process with an unbounded write-freeze reconciliation loop
symptoms: Publishing stalls, frontend Thrift reads time out, and end-user throughput falls far below 70 requests per second. All pods remain Running and Ready. MongoDB reads, collection contents, indexes, and Kubernetes routing remain normal; post inserts queue behind the global administrative write freeze.
why_hard: The visible timeout is at the frontend, while the durable write lock is in the post datastore and its owner is an idle detached Mongo shell inside the media datastore. No Deployment, ConfigMap, database schema, or application record differs from the stock installation. Releasing the lock produces an entirely healthy 120-second SLO window, then the coordinator silently reacquires it after 210-215 seconds. Restarting the publishing services leaves both the lock and coordinator intact; restarting only the affected database leaves the remote coordinator intact.
expected_agent_pitfalls: Treat generic frontend transport timeouts as a Thrift pool, DNS, or publishing-service problem
Conclude that MongoDB is healthy from successful reads, normal documents and indexes, and a successful ping
Release the administrative lock, observe immediate recovery and a healthy rolling SLO window, and finish before the delayed regression
Restart the affected services or datastore without tracing the idle administrative session to the remote media datastore container
Look for a Job, CronJob, sidecar, ConfigMap or altered deployment to explain the repeated maintenance operation
mitigation_summary: Trace the Mongo shell session's source address to media-mongodb, terminate the detached snapshot coordinator and remove its maintenance files, then release all post-store fsync lock references. No saved manifests or private data are needed.
